core_obligations: Write the group of homotopy classes of maps into the complex over the base ring as the corresponding group over the target ring applied to the base changed source (proof lines 13932-13936).
Use flatness of the ring map to see that tensoring with the target ring preserves acyclicity, so that the target side vanishing condition applies (proof lines 13936-13937).
Conclude that the vanishing condition holds over the base ring, which is K-injectivity there (proof lines 13937-13938).

Use exactness of the base change (proof lines 13936-13937).
Read off K-injectivity over the base (proof lines 13937-13938).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that K-injectivity descends along a flat ring map, and the proof is a 6-line argument that rewrites the defining vanishing condition by adjunction. It identifies the group of homotopy classes of maps into the complex over the base ring with the corresponding group over the target ring after tensoring the source with the target ring, using the tensor-restriction adjunction together with exactness of the base change; the vanishing condition defining K-injectivity on the target therefore pulls back to the base. The two ingredients — the adjunction and the exactness of tensoring with the flat algebra — are exactly what the flatness hypothesis is needed for, and both are displayed.
